title: Vizmatic
summary: Lit curves gather into the wordmark and let go again, as a seamless ten-second loop.

title: Downhill, one step at a time
summary: Real gradient descent on a two-basin loss surface: two starts 0.12 apart travel together, then finish in different minima.

title: The rules are exact, the future is not
summary: The Lorenz system integrated with real numbers: two starts a hair apart part ways, then 72 fill the butterfly.

title: Twelve coin flips, nine hundred times
summary: A Galton board settles into a histogram that meets the Gaussian curve, with mean and deviation measured from the balls.

title: FlashAttention: tiling beats memory bandwidth
summary: Online running-max softmax streams K and V blocks through fast on-chip SRAM without materializing the N by N attention matrix in HBM.

title: io_uring: shared rings, fewer syscalls
summary: Userspace and the kernel exchange requests through shared submission and completion rings. Batching reduces submission syscalls; an awake SQPOLL thread can avoid them until a wakeup is needed.

title: SVD: reorient, stretch, reorient
summary: A unit sphere becomes an ellipsoid under a real 3D matrix, then collapses exactly to rank two. SVD separates orthogonal factors, which may rotate or reflect, from singular-value scaling.

title: A drawing is a sum of circles
summary: A real Fourier transform of an ampersand, redrawn by a chain of rotating arrows as the term count grows from 1 to 200.

title: Every claim needs a receipt
summary: Retrieved source passages wire directly to generated clauses, catching an unsupported claim when its citation thread snaps.

title: Eight GPUs, one ring, bounded transfer
summary: An ideal eight-GPU ring combines seven reduce-scatter hops with seven all-gather hops. Per-rank transfer volume stays bounded, while latency and utilization depend on topology and workload.

title: One expired key can take down the database
summary: An illustrative one-process batch model turns 480 cache misses into duplicate database queries, then coalesces them with an in-memory key lock. A linear timeline compares the assumed latencies.

title: Paxos: two majorities share an acceptor
summary: Real single-decree Paxos with lost and late messages: a proposer that hears of two accepted proposals takes the value of the higher number, and 400 random runs never choose two values.

title: Attention routes context where grammar alone cannot
summary: Hand-authored 4D query, key, and value vectors illustrate attention. Matrix and bars share the same ten-key softmax distribution, with omitted keys grouped explicitly.

title: A forecast is a range
summary: A small forecaster reads a seeded metric and draws its own past errors again as 1,000 possible futures. Two bands hold half of them and 9 of 10, the truth lands inside the wide one 43 times of 48, and 1,000 runs show how often that band is right.

title: The grid bends, its right angles survive
summary: A grid unfolds under z squared and curls into a disk under a Mobius map, with the angle at every crossing measured live.

title: A matrix moves the whole plane
summary: A grid under one matrix: basis arrows, the determinant as area, and the two directions that stay on their lines.

title: One point, two shadows
summary: A point sweeps the unit circle, sine and cosine trace themselves, and the formula collapses into Euler's identity.

title: A beam keeps more than one path
summary: In a normalized three-token toy model, greedy decoding picks a sequence with probability 0.18. A beam of two keeps an alternative prefix and finds one with probability 0.324.

title: Move the pieces, keep the square
summary: A proof by rearrangement: four triangles slide inside a square, and the leftover area writes the theorem.

title: Sine, from what it does at zero
summary: Polynomials hug the sine curve further out as each term grows in, with the trusted range measured live.

title: Why we rebuilt the renderer
summary: A five-slide engineering talk about per-frame layout and timeline sampling. Historical measurements use different demos on one laptop, not a controlled speedup comparison.
